notes:
I couldn't write these notes because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt to fetch pages from enduringword.com, biblehub.com (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill), preceptaustin.org and netbible.org failed because of a bug in my code. When I tried to fix it, the research tool said I had used up my calls for this turn. So I haven't read a single page on Isaiah 12.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Any notes I wrote now would break that rule, so there are none.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start over in this order:
1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub or StudyLight, then Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** searches on the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites. Verse 3 (water from the springs of salvation) and verse 2 (God as "my salvation") are the most likely places for differences, but I'll only say so if the sources do.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, and New Advent (Church Fathers), Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, such as how verse 3 relates to baptism or the liturgy. I'll include popular modern teaching only if the sites actually discuss it.

The notes will be verse by verse, with a URL for every point, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
